title: Priority lending pools: controlled burst borrowing and reclaim for Dedicated tenants
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a controlled 'Priority Lending Pool' feature that lets Dedicated tenants borrow short-term extra GPU headroom from a managed reservoir when their reserved capacity is exhausted. The feature must enforce tenant isolation, repayment rules, and automated reclaiming to protect SLAs while improving observed success rates for transient spikes. This PRD defines the product scope, requirements, acceptance criteria, metrics, rollout and rollback plans, and open questions.
background: Customers on Dedicated often hit transient traffic spikes (sync-heavy inference bursts) that exceed their reserved capacity and lead to throttling or degraded latency. Current fallback options (cross-tenant backfill or best-effort opportunistic capacity) either violate isolation expectations or produce unpredictable latency. A bounded lending mechanism provides predictable, measurable short-term relief without permanent reservation changes.
goals: Allow tenants to opt into a controlled short-term borrow policy that grants additional qps/headroom from a shared lending pool
Ensure borrowing respects tenant isolation guarantees and does not violate other tenants' SLAs
Provide transparent repayment/crediting and billing signals so customers understand cost and impact
Fail closed gracefully: if lending pool is exhausted, existing SLO degradation behaviors remain unchanged
Expose observability for borrowed usage, repayment status, and reclaim events in Console and telemetry
non_goals: Automatic permanent increases to a tenant's reserved capacity without an explicit purchase or contract change
Replacing existing preemptive eviction or hard preemption primitives for multi-tenant contention
Addressing multi-region data residency differences in initial rollout; VPC/private will be considered in follow-ups
requirements: R1: Admin-configurable lending pools - operators can create named lending pools with total capacity, per-tenant max-borrow and min-reserve thresholds
R2: Tenant opt-in flag - tenants must explicitly opt into borrowing; default off

R3: Borrow creditline and repayment rules - each borrow operation creates a creditline entry with TTL (repayment window) and a repayment schedule; auto-repayment occurs by reducing future burst eligibility or billing as 'burst credits'
R4: Reclaim heuristics - runtime must implement soft reclaim (rate-limited reduction) and hard reclaim (eviction) tiers with configurable grace windows tied to tenant priority
R5: Billing and metering - borrowed tokens and repayment adjustments must be visible in billing exports and Console usage views with per-tenant line items
R6: Observability - Console shows borrowed capacity, active creditlines, repayment timeline, reclaim events, and per-route latency impact; traces annotate borrow events
R7: SLO Safeguards - lending cannot reduce the reserved minimum capacity below a configured minimum; pool-level admission control ensures aggregate reserved SLOs remain satisfied
R8: Testing and canary controls - feature gated by org-level flag and rollout policy for canary tenants and zones
R9: Audit and compliance - all borrow/reclaim events recorded in audit log with initiator (system/operator), timestamps, and final outcome
R10: Operator controls - ability to drain a pool, force-reclaim active creditlines, and view repayment ledger
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Create a lending pool via operator API with totalCapacity=1000 qps and perTenantMax=200 qps; pool appears in Console
AC2: A tenant with reserved capacity 100 qps that opts in can borrow 50 qps during a spike; metrics show borrowed=50, latency SLO maintained within degradation budget
AC3: Borrow entries include repayment window (e.g., 30 minutes) and are visible in both Console and billing export CSV

AC4: When pool available capacity drops below threshold (10%), new borrow requests are rejected and caller receives standardized error code (ERR_LENDING_POOL_FULL) and fallback behavior is the same as pre-feature path
AC5: Operator can force-reclaim a tenant's active creditline; runtime performs soft reclaim over 60s by throttling borrowed capacity and emits audit log event with outcome
AC6: In canary rollout (5% of tenants), logging, metrics, and trace annotations for borrow/reclaim do not add more than 5% overhead to request latency p95 compared to baseline
AC7: Billing export reconciles borrowed qps into a 'burst_credits' column and monthly billing reflects consumption for any tenant that exceeded reservation during the billing period
AC8: Security review signoff completed and audit log schema approved before wider rollout
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal operator test cluster (1 week) to validate operator APIs and reclaim hooks. Phase 2: Canary with 5% Dedicated tenants in non-critical zones (4 weeks) with close telemetry. Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 50% with opt-in campaign and support docs (6 weeks). Phase 4: Full general availability after billing reconciliation tests and security signoff. Feature toggle allows immediate global rollback.
metrics: M1: Borrow success rate (per-tenant and pool) - target > 99% for accepted borrow requests
M2: Fraction of spikes mitigated by lending (%) - relative to baseline spikes that resulted in throttling
M4: Number of forced reclaims per week
M5: Billing reconciliation delta between ledger and invoice - target < 0.5%
M6: Latency p95 change for borrowers during borrow period - target < 10% increase vs reserved-only baseline
risks: RISK: Lending pool could be abused as a backdoor to permanently increase throughput; mitigations: strict per-tenant caps and repayment windows, billing signaling, and operator alerts
RISK: Reclaim operations could cause sudden latency spikes for affected tenants; mitigations: staged soft reclaim, backoff heuristics, and playbook for on-call
RISK: Complexity of repayment semantics could confuse customers; mitigations: clear Console UX, billing examples, and migration guides
RISK: Cross-tenant telemetry leak if traces expose tenant identifiers during pooled borrowing; mitigations: ensure trace redaction and tenant-scoped views only
qa_plan: QA1: Unit and integration tests for operator API, creditline ledger, and reclaim logic
QA2: Load tests simulating 100s of concurrent borrowers with random repayment windows to verify pool admission controls
QA3: Chaos tests: force node loss while borrowers active to validate graceful reclaim and audit trails
QA4: End-to-end billing test comparing ledger output to invoicing pipeline for a synthetic month
QA5: Security pen-test focusing on audit log integrity and access control to operator APIs
open_questions: Q1: What is the canonical currency for expressing borrowed capacity (qps, token-rate, or GPU-seconds)? Ops prefers qps but some models are better expressed as tokens/minute.
Q2: Should repayment be enforced via billing-only (charge extra) or via enforced reduction of future burst eligibility? Can we support both as a tenant preference?
Q3: For multi-zone Dedicated deployments, should lending pools be zonal-only or cross-zone with region-level coordination?
Q4: What SLA language do we publish regarding borrowed capacity (is borrowed capacity covered by the tenant SLA or explicitly excluded)?
Q5: What default per-tenant max-borrow value is reasonable for new tenants that opt in (10%, 50% of reservation, or absolute 100 qps)?
